references.text: Parallel passage in Matthew where Jesus says that whoever does his heavenly Father's will is his brother, sister, and mother. The same event and message: spiritual kinship through obedience to God's will surpasses biological kinship.
Parallel passage in Mark where Jesus asks who his mother and brothers are, and answers that those who do God's will are his family. This is the same account retold in another gospel tradition.
Jesus says that those who hear God's word and keep it are more blessed than the woman who bore and nursed him. Same theme: spiritual obedience to God's word is more important than biological ties.
Jesus calls his disciples friends if they do what he commands them. Shows that the relationship with Jesus is conditioned on obedience to his words, in line with Luke 8:21.
James urges believers to be doers of the word, not merely hearers. This directly reflects Jesus' words that his family consists of those who hear God's word and do it.
Whoever does God's will remains forever. The theme of doing God's will as a mark of true belonging to God aligns with Jesus' words in Luke 8:21.
Whoever keeps God's commandments abides in God, and God in him. Keeping God's word is the sign of fellowship with God, just as Jesus defines his family as those who hear and do God's word.

Jesus says that not everyone who says 'Lord, Lord' will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only the one who does his heavenly Father's will. Same emphasis on doing God's will as the criterion for belonging.
Jesus says that disciples are blessed if they do what they know. Emphasizes that acting on God's word—not merely hearing it—is essential.
Jesus is not ashamed to call believers his brothers. The spiritual kinship between Jesus and those who belong to him confirms the message in Luke 8:21 that Jesus' true family are the believers.

Those whom God foreknew, he predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son, so that the Son might be the firstborn among many brothers. Believers are called Jesus' siblings by living according to God's will.
